handoffs.notes: FuzeInfra#499/#500. Source is the hand-off Secret from #166/#183 (a single `password` key, unrotated since 2026-07-08). The consumer does not consume a bare password: mendys-prod/mendys-secrets holds a composed DATABASE_URL, so format is postgres-url. The re-seal that resolved #499 by hand (MendysRobotics#273) changed exactly this one encryptedData key and left the other 23 alone — which is why the publisher must kubeseal --merge-into and must never regenerate the manifest.

DISABLED 2026-08-20. izzywdev/FuzeQuality cannot be resolved — `gh repo clone` returns "Could not resolve to a Repository with the name 'izzywdev/FuzeQuality'" and the session's repo-attach reports no access, so the repo is deleted, renamed, or was never created under that name. GraphQL returns the same error for absent and not-visible, so this does not by itself prove deletion. It was the ONLY entry still failing after FuzeInfra#596, and a permanently undeliverable entry makes publish-sealed-handoff exit 1 on EVERY run — which trains people to ignore a workflow whose entire value is that a red run means something. Note the fuzequality NAMESPACE does exist in-cluster and its Argo Application syncs from FuzeFront's revision under project fuzefront, so whatever runs there is not deployed from a FuzeQuality repo at all. Re-enable once the repo is confirmed to exist and be reachable. ORIGINAL NOTE FOLLOWS. FuzeInfra#541. URGENT: FuzeFront#633 is held open specifically because merging it before this secret exists would CrashLoop the FuzeQuality backend pod. Source: the bearer token the fuzefront/fuzefront-registration Secret holds (created by FuzeFront's consumer-registration-seed post-upgrade Job). format=raw seals the token verbatim. The manifest is created fresh if absent — FuzeQuality has no prior sealed-secrets file at this path.

FuzeInfra#541. The @fuzefront/onboarding-kit init container requires this bearer token in the pod's own namespace. Source: fuzefront/fuzefront-registration key token (created by FuzeFront's consumer-registration-seed Job). Sealed raw for the fuzeplan namespace.

FuzeInfra#541. New consumer repo. Argo Application registration (argocd-register workflow) must be triggered separately after FuzeDeploy's deploy/argocd/ is wired. This handoff creates the sealed manifest from scratch — the path will not exist until the first run.

FuzeInfra#541. New consumer repo. BRANCH IS `master`, NOT `main` — FuzeX is the only consumer here whose default branch is master, and `gh repo clone --branch main` failed with a message blaming GH_TOKEN (FuzeInfra#595). FuzeX's ingress is hostless/disabled pending DNS setup — do not flip registration.enabled in values-prod.yaml until fuzex.prod.fuzefront.com is confirmed live. prune:false on the Argo Application (design-frame PVC must not be pruned). This handoff creates the sealed manifest from scratch.

FuzeInfra#541. New consumer repo. fuzecall-control-plane/CONTROL_PLANE_API_KEY must also be sealed before the pod can start — that is an operator-supplied secret not in this handoff. Ingress is disabled+hostless pending DNS. This handoff creates the sealed manifest from scratch.
FuzeInfra#541. New consumer repo. Ingress disabled+hostless pending DNS (fuzefinance.prod.fuzefront.com). This handoff creates the sealed manifest from scratch.
FuzeInfra#541. New consumer repo. Host deliberately unset — ingress.host must be decided before enabling. This handoff creates the sealed manifest from scratch.

FuzeInfra#541. Registration is off in FuzeBI today (registration.enabled=false in values-prod.yaml). Sealing the token now so the secret is present when registration is switched on — the init container is fail-closed and the pod will not start without it. Ingress disabled+hostless pending DNS (fuzebi.prod.fuzefront.com). This handoff creates the sealed manifest from scratch.

Added 2026-08-20. FuzeMerchandize had NO entry here at all, so nothing had ever delivered it a registration token — while its own deploy/argocd/README.md describes the register init container as unconditional and fail-closed, i.e. the pod cannot start without this Secret. A fail-closed consumer with no delivery path can never come up, and nothing reported it: an ABSENT registry entry produces no failure, only silence. That is the same shape as FuzeInfra#552 — the missing thing is invisible precisely because it is missing. Creates the sealed manifest from scratch; the path does not exist in that repo yet.
